transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. That pattern—running for a bit then stopping, only to restart after cooling—is classic overheating protection kicking in. The dryer detects it’s getting too hot (usually because airflow is restricted) and cuts power to prevent damage; once it cools down, it resets and tries again. The most common cause is blocked airflow. Please check these two things:
1. Clean the lint filter thoroughly. If your model has a second filter or a condenser unit inside the door flap (common in vented/condenser models), remove and rinse that under cold water too, then let it dry completely before refitting.
2. Check the vent hose going out the window. Ensure it isn’t kinked, crushed, or blocked by lint at the wall outlet. If these are clear and the problem persists, we’ll look at whether the blower fan is working properly or if there’s an issue with the thermal cut-out itself.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok unplugged. filter i clean every time. just checked the hose and its kinked n crushed behind the dryer, i pushed it back further recently. also cabinet gets really hot before it stops

That explains it perfectly. A kinked or crushed vent hose restricts airflow, causing the air to get trapped and the machine to overheat rapidly—hence why the cabinet gets so hot before it cuts out. Please straighten the hose fully so there are no bends or crushes behind the dryer, and ensure the wall outlet is clear of lint. 1. Plug the dryer back in.
2. Run a normal drying cycle with a typical load.
3. Stay nearby to see if it completes without stopping. If it runs through normally, the kink was the only issue. If it still cuts out after about 10 minutes even with the hose straight and clear, we will need to check if the blower fan is actually moving air or if a thermal component has failed.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok will straighten it n try a cycle. do i need to pull the dryer out to do it? its a tight fit

You don't necessarily need to pull the whole machine out. Once you've straightened it out, plug it back in and run that cycle. If it runs through without stopping, the kink was most likely the cause. If it still cuts out after 10 minutes even with a clear path, we'll need to check if the blower fan is actually spinning or if there's an internal blockage.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok will try it now. just to check, ok to run it with the hose straightened but still tight behind the dryer?

The key is that air can flow freely through the entire length of the hose and out the window. Please go ahead and run a normal drying cycle now. Keep an ear out for whether the drum is spinning properly and if you feel strong airflow coming from the vent outside (or hear it blowing). If the machine completes the cycle without cutting out, that suggests the kink was the problem. If it still cuts out after about 10 minutes despite the hose being clear, we will need to investigate whether the internal blower fan is actually working or if there is a blockage further inside.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
ok but its still crushed a bit behind so not sure thats clear. its been going hot again. want me to just keep running it like that?

No, please do not keep running it like that. A crushed hose is still restricting airflow, which means the machine will overheat again—this time potentially causing damage or creating a fire risk from trapped lint heating up. You need to create a clear path for the air. Because it’s tight behind there, you may need to pull the dryer out just enough (a few inches) to fully straighten and uncrush that section of the hose. The air must be able to flow freely all the way to the window. Once you’ve done that:
1. Unplug the machine again.
2. Ensure the hose is smooth and clear for its entire length.
3. Plug it back in and run a cycle. If you cannot move the dryer enough to fix the crush, or if it still cuts out after 10 minutes with the hose fully straight, we will need to check if the internal blower fan is working properly.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok stopped it. will pull it out a bit n straighten the hose then try again. its hot in here tho, shud i leave it to cool first?

Yes, please leave it unplugged until the cabinet has cooled down completely. It is safer and more comfortable for you, and it ensures the thermal cut-out resets properly before you try again. Once it is cool:
1. Pull the dryer out just enough to fully straighten that crushed section of the hose so air can flow freely.
2. Plug it back in.
3. Run a cycle with a normal load (not too small, not overloaded).
4. Stay nearby and listen: does the drum spin normally, and do you feel strong airflow coming from the vent outside? If it runs through without stopping again, the crushed hose was the only issue. If it still cuts out after about 10 minutes even with a clear hose, we will need to check if the internal blower fan is actually working.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
